description: Verified battery-test protocol records used by the Interactive Leaks calibration dataset. Protocol constants include only conditions supported by cited methodology documentation. Device- or review-specific conditions belong on measurement records.

protocols.name: Wi-Fi Web Browsing Test
protocols.workload_description: Automated browsing workload using a mix of internet pages that change every 30 seconds.

notes: Notebookcheck describes the WLAN runtime test as using adjusted display brightness of approximately 150 cd/m².
The documented v1.3 script uses HTML5 and JavaScript and calls up a changing mix of internet pages every 30 seconds.
The methodology page states that power-saving measures are activated for the WLAN test.
Browser identity, browser version, refresh behavior, display resolution, signal quality and other review-specific conditions must not be inferred from this protocol record.

sources.title: How does Notebookcheck test laptops and smartphones? A behind-the-scenes look into our review process

limitations: The methodology documentation does not establish every condition needed for a complete device power model.
Approximately 150 cd/m² must not be represented as an exact 150 cd/m² device measurement.
Review-specific settings must be stored on individual measurement records when available.

protocols.name: Cellular Web Browsing Battery Test
protocols.workload_description: Continuous web browsing over a cellular connection from a fully charged battery until the device runs out of power.

connectivity.cellular_generation: 5G for 5G-capable devices; otherwise dependent on device/test

notes: Tom's Guide documents setting each phone display to 150 nits before its battery test.
The phone browses the web over cellular until the battery is depleted.
Current methodology documentation specifies 5G for 5G-capable devices.
Tom's Guide may test multiple refresh-rate settings, so the actual refresh configuration must be recorded on the individual measurement when known.
No protocol version is assigned because the reviewed methodology documentation does not provide a formal version identifier.

sources.title: How Tom's Guide tests and reviews smartphones

limitations: Cellular signal conditions are not established as a universal constant by the methodology page.
Refresh-rate configuration can vary between reported device results.
Browser and browser version are not encoded as protocol constants here.
The absence of a formal protocol version requires measurement dates and source pages to remain attached to observations.

protocols.name: Calibrated Battery Use Cases
protocols.workload_description: Controlled single-activity battery tests performed with standardized device and environmental parameters.

connectivity.signal_conditions: controlled network conditions documented generally, exact parameters unresolved in this seed record

notes: DXOMARK describes calibrated use cases as using the same settings and application parameters across tested phones.
Display brightness is documented at 200 cd/m².
Speaker level is documented at 60 dB when applicable.
DXOMARK documents calibrated use cases including video streaming over cellular and Wi-Fi, video playback, music streaming, gaming, calls and idle.
DXOMARK states that its battery protocols are updated over time.
Methodology pages have documented different speaker measurement distances at different times; therefore measurement distance is intentionally not encoded as a timeless protocol constant here.
Individual DXOMARK workload measurements should identify their specific workload rather than being stored only under the broad calibrated-use-case protocol.

sources.title: How DXOMARK tests the smartphone battery experience

limitations: No formal protocol version is assigned because DXOMARK explicitly updates its methodology and the reviewed pages do not provide a single stable version identifier suitable for all historical measurements.
Historical measurements must be associated with their test date and original result page before calibration use.
Speaker measurement distance must be resolved per applicable methodology period if it becomes relevant to a model.
Exact network parameters, application versions and other workload-specific conditions require further evidence before becoming calibration constants.
